::: {.callout-important}
## Summary

- **Why:** my conda environments on Pegasus were deleted in early October 2026, so `orthofinder_env` had to be rebuilt before the SATURN benchmarking work.
- **The old conda (4.10.1, from 2021) can no longer build environments from conda-forge:** it fails while downloading the channel index. I switched to **micromamba**, a small stand-alone conda replacement.
- **The bigger problem was the `/nethome` limit**, not the tool. Installs failed with `No space left on device` even after freeing 180 GB, which points to a limit on the **number of files** rather than their size.
- **Fix:** keep the package cache on `/scratch`, and install a **lean environment**: OrthoFinder plus only the tools it actually runs, skipping the ~150-package plotting/GUI stack.
- **Result:** OrthoFinder 3.1.0 runs end to end in an LSF job (3-species test). The working recipe and job-script header are in [How to use it later](#how-to-use-it-later).
:::

# Key terms

| Term | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| **Environment (env)** | A folder holding one set of installed tools and their dependencies, kept separate from other projects. |
| **conda / micromamba** | Two programs that build envs from the same channels. micromamba is a single binary, much faster, and handles today's very large channel index well. |
| **Channel index** | The catalogue of available packages a channel publishes (conda-forge's is now very large). |
| **Package cache** | Where downloaded packages are unpacked before being copied into an env. Normally inside the conda/micromamba folder on `/nethome`. |
| **File-count (inode) limit** | A cap on how many files a user can store, separate from the cap on total size. An env is tens of thousands of small files. |
| `--no-deps` | Install one package without pulling in its dependencies. |
| **LSF project / queue** | Pegasus job settings: `-P` (which allocation to charge) and `-q` (which group of nodes). |

: Terms used in this entry. {#tbl-terms}

# 1. What went wrong, in order

Each problem only appeared once the one before it was fixed. Exact error messages are kept so this page turns up in a search next time.

## 1.1 conda 4.10.1 cannot download the conda-forge index

```
Collecting package metadata (repodata.json): failed
requests.exceptions.ChunkedEncodingError: ("Connection broken: InvalidChunkLength(got length b'', 0 bytes read)", ...)
```

**Cause.** Old conda downloads each channel's full index as one huge file. conda-forge's index has grown enormously since 2021, and the connection drops partway through. It failed the same way on a second try with longer timeouts, so this is not a one-off. micromamba fetches the index in small pieces and had no trouble.

**Fix.** Use micromamba for new envs; leave the old Anaconda base in place for `saturn_protein`.

## 1.2 Pasting into the micromamba installer

The official installer (`"${SHELL}" <(curl -L micro.mamba.pm/install.sh)`) asks questions. I pasted it together with the next few commands, and those lines were read as answers. The result was a binary inside a folder literally named `source ~` and a broken `micromamba initialize` block in `~/.bashrc`.

**Fix.** Rename the folder before touching it (`mv -- "$HOME/source ~" "$HOME/junk_paste"`), move the binary to `~/.local/bin/`, delete the `.bashrc` block and run `micromamba shell init --shell bash --root-prefix ~/micromamba`.

::: {.callout-warning}
Never run `rm -rf source ~` on a folder with that name: unquoted, the shell reads it as "delete `source` and my whole home directory". Rename first, then delete. And never paste a multi-line block into an interactive installer.
:::

The installer can be skipped entirely; see [Install micromamba](#install-micromamba).

## 1.3 `No space left on device` while unpacking

```
critical libmamba filesystem error: cannot create directories: No space left on device [/nethome/kxw755/micromamba/pkgs/...]
critical libmamba Found incorrect downloads. Aborting
```

All 752 MB downloaded, then unpacking ~200 packages failed. `df` showed 21 TB free on `/nethome`, so this is my personal limit, not a full disk.

- Freeing **180 GB** (two leftover GeneExt `merge.bam` files) did **not** help.
- A 2 GB test write and 2,000 small test files both succeeded.
- `mmlsquota` is not available to users on Pegasus, so I could not read the limits directly.

**Most likely cause (not confirmed):** a per-user **file-count** limit. My home holds ~245,000 files, ~205,000 of them in the 2021 Anaconda base (Spyder, Jupyter, Navigator…), and a full OrthoFinder env adds tens of thousands more. `conda clean --all` only removed ~660 files, because nearly all of those files belong to the base install itself.

## 1.4 Moving the cache to `/scratch` helped, but not enough

With `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS`/`MAMBA_PKGS_DIRS` pointing at `/scratch`, every package unpacked fine. It then failed while copying files into the env on `/nethome`:

```
error libmamba Unexpected error while linking package 'qt-main': filesystem error: cannot copy: No space left on device
```

**Cause.** `qt-main` is a GUI toolkit with a very large number of small files. OrthoFinder does not need it to run; it comes in through optional tree-plotting dependencies.

**Fix: a lean env.** Install the run-time tools first, then OrthoFinder with `--no-deps`. This skipped 151 packages (Qt, X11, fonts, IQ-TREE, RAxML, BLAST, MMseqs2, FAMSA…), none of which my settings use:

| Skipped | Matters for my runs? |
|---|---|
| FAMSA (OrthoFinder 3's default aligner) | No, I use `-A mafft` |
| IQ-TREE, RAxML | No, I use `-T fasttree` |
| BLAST, MMseqs2 | No, DIAMOND is the default search |
| Qt, PyQt, X11, fonts | No, only for drawing trees |
| Biopython, ete3 | **Yes**, added back by hand (next section) |

: What the lean install leaves out. {#tbl-skipped}

## 1.5 Two Python modules added back

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'Bio'
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ete3'
```

Biopython installs normally. ete3 was installed with `pip install --no-deps` (plus `six`) so it does not pull Qt back in. OrthoFinder only uses ete3 to read and write tree files.

## 1.6 LSF and job-script problems

```
Error: kxw755 account has multiple projects: dark_genes transcriptomics.
general: Queue has been closed. Job not submitted.
micromamba: command not found
```

- Every job now needs `#BSUB -P dark_genes` (or `transcriptomics`).
- The `general` queue is closed (as of Oct 2026). `normal` had the shortest wait; `bigmem` is still open. **Old scripts that use `-q general` will fail.**
- Batch jobs do not read `~/.bashrc`, so micromamba must be called by its full path inside job scripts (see the [job-script header](#job-header)).

## 1.7 Test runs: two species is not enough

A 2-species test (500 Pdam + 500 Acer proteins) built orthogroups and orthologues, then stopped at the last step:

```
ERROR in parallel process, exiting.
```

with an empty `Phylogenetic_Hierarchical_Orthogroups/N0.tsv`. OrthoFinder cannot root a species tree with only two species, so it has nothing to build hierarchical orthogroups from. Adding 500 *N. vectensis* proteins gave a clean run:

| Measure | 3-species test |
|---|---|
| Species / genes | 3 / 1,500 |
| Genes in orthogroups | 701 |
| Hierarchical orthogroups (`N1.tsv`) | 115 |
| Run time (4 cores, `normal` queue) | 68 s |
| stderr | empty |

: Final test run. {#tbl-test}

With three species the root node file is `N1.tsv` rather than `N0.tsv`; real runs with more species produce `N0.tsv` as usual.

# 2. The working recipe

## Install micromamba (once) {#install-micromamba}

Skips the interactive installer:

```bash
cd ~
curl -Ls https://micro.mamba.pm/api/micromamba/linux-64/latest | tar -xvj bin/micromamba
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && mv ~/bin/micromamba ~/.local/bin/ && rmdir ~/bin 2>/dev/null
~/.local/bin/micromamba shell init --shell bash --root-prefix ~/micromamba
source ~/.bashrc
```

## Build `orthofinder_env`

```bash
# package cache on scratch (keeps half the files off /nethome); unpack one package at a time
export CONDA_PKGS_DIRS=/scratch/dark_genes/mamba_pkgs
export MAMBA_PKGS_DIRS=/scratch/dark_genes/mamba_pkgs
export MAMBA_EXTRACT_THREADS=1    # micromamba 2.x dropped the --extract-threads flag

# 1. run-time tools only
micromamba create -y -n orthofinder_env -c conda-forge -c bioconda --strict-channel-priority \
  python=3.11 numpy scipy scikit-learn rich diamond mcl fasttree mafft

# 2. OrthoFinder itself, without its optional dependency stack
micromamba install -y -n orthofinder_env -c conda-forge -c bioconda --no-deps orthofinder=3.1.0

# 3. the two Python modules it needs
micromamba install -y -n orthofinder_env -c conda-forge --strict-channel-priority biopython
micromamba run -n orthofinder_env pip install --no-deps ete3 six

# 4. check
micromamba activate orthofinder_env
orthofinder -h | head -3
which diamond mcl mafft FastTree

unset CONDA_PKGS_DIRS MAMBA_PKGS_DIRS MAMBA_EXTRACT_THREADS
```

Installed versions: OrthoFinder 3.1.0, DIAMOND 2.2.8, MCL 22.282, MAFFT 7.526, FastTree 2.2.0, Python 3.11.17, ete3 3.1.3.

# 3. How to use it later {#how-to-use-it-later}

## Job-script header {#job-header}

Use this in every OrthoFinder job; change only the name, cores, wall time and input folder:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#BSUB -J of_run
#BSUB -P dark_genes
#BSUB -q normal                 # or bigmem; general is closed
#BSUB -n 16
#BSUB -W 120:00
#BSUB -o /scratch/dark_genes/<run>/of.%J.out
#BSUB -e /scratch/dark_genes/<run>/of.%J.err

# batch jobs don't read .bashrc: call micromamba by full path
export MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX=/nethome/kxw755/micromamba
eval "$(/nethome/kxw755/.local/bin/micromamba shell hook --shell bash)"
micromamba activate orthofinder_env
which orthofinder diamond mcl mafft FastTree   # logs the tool paths

orthofinder -f <dir_with_only_protein_fastas> -t 16 -a 16 -M msa -A mafft -T fasttree
```

Rules of thumb:

- The input folder should hold **only** protein FASTAs. Job scripts and logs in it trigger `Files have been ignored as they don't appear to be FASTA files`, and results land inside it (`<input>/OrthoFinder/Results_<date>/`).
- Test with **at least three species**.
- The [multi-species OrthoFinder pipeline](../pipelines/orthofinder-multispecies.qmd) still activates the env with `conda activate`; its job block needs the micromamba lines above before it will run again.

## Back up the recipe

```bash
mkdir -p ~/env_backups
micromamba env export -n orthofinder_env > ~/env_backups/orthofinder_env.yml
echo "pip install --no-deps ete3==3.1.3 six==1.17.0" > ~/env_backups/orthofinder_env_pip.txt
conda env export -n saturn_protein > ~/env_backups/saturn_protein.yml
```

`env export` does not record the pip packages, hence the separate note. Copy `~/env_backups` off Pegasus: `/nethome` is not backed up, and a future wipe could take these files too.

## If it breaks again

| Symptom | First thing to try |
|---|---|
| `micromamba: command not found` in a job | Use the full-path activation block above |
| `No space left on device` during a create | Cache on `/scratch` (`CONDA_PKGS_DIRS`/`MAMBA_PKGS_DIRS`) and the lean install; if it still fails, ask HPC support for my `/nethome` usage and limits |
| `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'X'` | `micromamba install -n orthofinder_env -c conda-forge X` (or `pip install --no-deps X` if it would pull in Qt) |
| `ERROR in parallel process` with empty `N0.tsv` | Probably a 2-species run; add a third species |
| FastTree `Illegal instruction` | Old node without AVX2; request newer nodes (seen during the Dark Genes runs) |
| `Queue has been closed` / `multiple projects` | Use `-q normal` or `bigmem`, and add `-P dark_genes` |

: Quick fixes. {#tbl-fixes}

# 4. Housekeeping and open items

- Deleted the two GeneExt `merge.bam` files (Pdam 110 GB, Acer 70 GB); they can be rebuilt from the per-library BAMs. Home went from ~825 GB to 645 GB.
- The four `possorted_genome_bam.bam` files (180 GB) are still in the GeneExt folders. Before deleting them: confirm where the GeneExt-extended GTFs were written, and that the raw FASTQs are backed up off Pegasus.
- The 2021 Anaconda base is ~205,000 files. Replacing it with micromamba alone would free most of the file allowance, but only after `saturn_protein` is exported and can be rebuilt.
- `~/.condarc` lists `defaults` and `nodefaults` as channels; they produce harmless warnings and can be removed.
- Next: run OrthoFinder on the SATURN benchmark proteomes.
